title: Groupe de Galois motivique : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
The page image is extremely faint. What can be read matches the following page (p.33) almost line for line, including the boxed heading 'Situation abstraite des double réseaux' and the boxed 'R ⊂ G_K' at the bottom. So this sheet is either a show-through/offset of p.33 or a first draft of it. The machine transcription of this page is mostly noise, and the reconstruction below follows the legible p.33 text.

Setting ('double lattices'):
- M is a ⊗-category (Tannakian) over a field k, with a diagram of fields k ⊂ K ⊂ L. (The diagram as drawn shows k and K both mapping into L.)
- T is a fibre functor over k, and T' is a fibre functor over K.
- φ: T⊗_k L ≅ T'⊗_K L is a ⊗-isomorphism over L.
- G = Aut_⊗(T) is an affine group over k. P = Isom_⊗(T_K, T') is a right G_K-torsor, and φ ∈ P(L).
- The data (G, P, φ) reconstruct (M, T, T', φ). This is Tannakian reconstruction applied to a pair of fibre functors.

The intended example is periods. k = Q, T is the Betti realisation, K is a number field or Q-bar, T' is the de Rham realisation, L = C, and φ is the period comparison isomorphism. Then P is the period torsor and φ is the 'period point'.

Trivial-torsor case:
- Choose ξ ∈ P(K) and write ξ = φg with g ∈ G(L).
- Changing ξ to ξa, with a ∈ G(K), replaces g by ga. So the class ġ ∈ G(L)/G(K) is canonical.
- (G, ġ) is equivalent to (G, P, φ).
- For a G-module V, the K-structure T'(V) inside V⊗_k L is g(V⊗_k K).
- Hence the 'double lattice' intersection is V ∩ T'(V) = {x ∈ V | g^{-1}x ∈ V⊗_k K}. This consists of the rational Betti classes whose periods are algebraic, i.e. those lying in the de Rham K-structure.

To analyse this intersection, Grothendieck takes the Zariski closure (over K) of the L-point γ, which he again calls T_K. For x ∈ V he notes T_K ⊂ Transp_{G_K}(x, γ), the transporter. For s, t in it, ts^{-1}x = x, i.e. ts^{-1} ∈ (G_x)_K. He then defines R as the closure of the image of T_K × T_K → G_K, (s,t) ↦ ts^{-1}. R is independent of the choice of g mod G(K), and R ⊂ G_K.

The point is that the algebraic relations satisfied by the period point (its K-Zariski closure) control which invariants and rational classes are forced. Combined with the previous page ('il faut compléter les conditions nécessaires par des conditions du type conj. de transcendance'), this is the germ of Grothendieck's period conjecture. In its later form: the K-Zariski closure of the period point is the whole torsor, equivalently dim = transcendence degree of the periods.
errors: Notation clash: T_K denotes both the base change of the fibre functor T and the Zariski closure of the L-point γ. This is not a mathematical error but is confusing.

Independence of R from the choice of g mod G(K) is asserted ('il est immédiat') without proof. Right multiplication by a ∈ G(K) translates the closure, and (s,t) ↦ ts^{-1} absorbs it. That is plausible but depends on left/right conventions that are not fixed on the page.
The machine transcription of this page is unreliable. The legible content is essentially that of p.33.

ideas.what: Two fibre functors over different fields k ⊂ K with a comparison isomorphism over L; the torsor P = Isom_⊗(T_K, T') with the point φ ∈ P(L) reconstructs the data
ideas.modern_name: period torsor / torsor of periods of a Tannakian category with Betti and de Rham fibre functors
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (via Deligne, André), Kontsevich–Zagier for the formal period torsor
ideas.where_published: Ideas appear in Deligne–Milne (1982), André 'Une introduction aux motifs' (2004), Kontsevich–Zagier 'Periods' (2001)

ideas.what: Canonical class ġ ∈ G(L)/G(K) and the description V ∩ T'(V) = {x | g^{-1}x ∈ V⊗K} of rational classes with algebraic periods
ideas.modern_name: period matrix modulo K-rational change of de Rham basis; 'double lattice' intersection
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical / folklore in the theory of periods

ideas.what: Zariski closure of the period point and the subvariety R = closure of {ts^{-1}} in G_K, linked to stabilizers G_x via transporters
ideas.modern_name: K-Zariski closure of the period point; Grothendieck period conjecture setup
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (period conjecture, c.1966, via Lang's footnote and André)
ideas.where_published: Mentioned in Lang, Introduction to Transcendental Numbers (1966); formulated in André's book

missed.claim: A 1965-dated archival manuscript develops the abstract 'double lattice' (period torsor) formalism. This documents Grothendieck's period conjecture setup at an early date, in Tannakian torsor language, before Saavedra and Deligne–Milne.
missed.quote: Situation abstraite des double réseaux ... P = Isom_⊗(T_K, T') torseur ... φ ∈ P(L)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It gives the historical origin of the torsor-of-periods formulation of the period conjecture and supports dating it to 1965–66. The idea itself is well known today.

deep.surprise_reason: The content (period torsor, period point, closure) is well known and attributed to Grothendieck in spirit. The archival interest is the early, explicit Tannakian-torsor formulation. This page is in any case a faint duplicate or draft of p.33.
transcription_corrections: The faint page reproduces p.33. The boxed top-right heading reads 'Situation abstraite des double réseaux'.
Line 1: 'M ⊗-catégorie sur corps k, diagramme de corps K, L, k', not 'Il ... K → L'.
'T foncteur fibre /k', 'T' ——— K [extension de k barré]'.
'φ: T⊗_k L ≃ T'⊗_K L ⊗-isom.' (the base field of T is k, not K).
'G = Aut_⊗(T) groupe affine sur k'; 'P = Isom_⊗(T_K, T') torseur à droite sous G_K'; 'φ ∈ P(L)' (not 'g ∈ P(L)').
The line read as 'H^1(G,T)' is actually 'Ces données permettent de reconstituer M, T, T', φ'.
'V ∩ T'(V) = {x ∈ V | g^{-1}x ∈ V⊗_k K}' rather than 'V_n T(K)'.
The bottom of the page carries the boxed 'R ⊂ G_K'.
